citation.description: build_bedrock_provider constructs BotoConfig(retries={'max_attempts': max(1,N), 'mode': 'adaptive'}, read_timeout=timeout_s, connect_timeout=timeout_s) and passes it via BedrockProvider(bedrock_client=client)

criteria.criterion: build_bedrock_provider threads a botocore.config.Config carrying retry and timeout settings derived from the same config values the Anthropic path uses, so llm_retry_max_attempts and timeout_s are honoured on Bedrock rather than ignored.

citation.description: Docstring at the set site documents: botocore max_attempts = total attempts incl. first = tenacity stop_after_attempt(N); timeout_s -> both read+connect (parity with single httpx.Timeout); llm_retry_max_wait_s deliberately unmapped

criteria.criterion: The retry-count and timeout SEMANTICS are documented where they are set, stating how the configured value maps onto botocore's attempt counting and onto connect vs read timeouts, so 'parity' names a defined behaviour rather than a matching integer.

citation.description: test_configured_retry_and_timeout_reach_the_botocore_client_config (lines 731-766) uses a spy boto3 session to assert the bedrock-runtime client is constructed with BotoConfig carrying the configured retry/timeout values; test_retry_attempts_below_one_clamp_to_a_single_attempt (lines 769-786) asserts clamping. Both would fail if builder reverted to bare BedrockProvider(region_name=region) since no session.client() call would be made.

criteria.criterion: A test asserts the constructed Bedrock client's config carries the configured values, and FAILS if the builder is reverted to BedrockProvider(region_name=region) with no config. Verify this by MUTATING the builder back and observing the test go RED.

citation.description: Section 'Retry / timeout posture on Bedrock: rebar-configured (adaptive retries + timeouts)' now describes the fixed behavior: build_bedrock_provider constructs the bedrock-runtime client with botocore Config from rebar's documented knobs; llm_retry_max_attempts and timeout DO apply. The old 'stock defaults apply' posture is gone. The eb6e alarm description (monitoring_eb6e.tf:75-77) also references the fix.

criteria.criterion: The runbook statement added by rebar:eb6e-f43a-e86b-443a — that botocore stock defaults apply and the two knobs do not reach Bedrock — is updated to describe the new behaviour, so the operator-facing text does not outlive the defect it describes.
